newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN OLOS TO HOLD FIRM IN FACE OF SCANDALS, FOMC.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN OLOS TO HOLD FIRM IN FACE OF SCANDALS, FOMC.

text.p: Belgian OLOs will trade quietly sideways on Tuesday ahead of the start of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting, ignoring the latest domestic political scandals, dealers said.

"There could be 10,000 scandals. It does not change anything. If they punished one person they would have to punish them all, so nothing will happen. One or two people may resign but that will be it," one trader said.
Police on Monday raided the office of Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt over allegations staff may have intervened in a tax probe involving some Belgian banks.
The raids came on top of an ongoing investigation into Belgium's French-speaking socialist party (PS), one of four which make up the country's ruling coalition government.

The tax probe raid slightly dented the Belgian franc, pushing it back to levels below 20.63 to the mark after it had staged an early morning recovery. The franc was at 20.6310/20 to the mark late on Monday, down from 20.6293/03 late on Friday and 20.6280/00 shortly before the news.
OLO traders said, however, they were not concerned, especially as the tax probe allegations had been headlined news in newspapers for several weeks.

Neither was the market likely to be moved if, as expected, the Walloon regional parliament moved late on Monday to lift the immunity of its President, Guy Spitaels, for questioning in the socialist party bribes probe. Spitaels has denied any wrongdoing and said he is open to questioning.
Attention would remain focused firmly on the start of the U.S. Fed's policy making Federal Open Market Committee meeting late in the session. The FOMC is due to meet again on Wednesday.
Against this background, a Belgian Treasury exchange auction was likely to draw little interest, one trader said.

At the auction, the Treasury is offering OLO lines 11 (9.00 pct, July 1998), 25 (5.00 pct, March 2001), 6 (9.00 pct, March 2003) and 26 (6.25 pct, March 2007) against 15 (6.75 pct, May 1997) and 8 (9.25 pct, Aug 1997)

"Maybe we will have some interest in the 11s," the trader said. He noted some domestic players were buying the short-end of the yield curve on Monday, although he said he would not while money market rates remained high because of the weak Belgian franc. The yield on OLO 11 (9.00 pct, July 1998) was 3.15 percent late on Monday compared with a yield on three-month Treasury certificates of around 3.07 percent.
One money market trader said rates remained above levels last week, but expected them to decline as fears of an imminent government collapse faded.
Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene on Monday rejected a suggestion from the youth wing of his party that the government should be reshuffled.
"There is consensus within the government that they have to get Belgium ready for economic and monetary union," the money market trader said.
He said a tight allotment of seven-day advances by the Belgian central bank on Monday had no impact on rates.
At the auction the bank cut liquidity to 9.975 billion from 15.500 billion francs against bids totalling 27 billion francs.
The trader said however banks were merely trying to get their hands on cheap money and the numbers did not reflect any shortage of cash in the market.
Advances auctions draw only a limited number of participants compared to four-day repos carried out by the Belgian National Bank with primary dealers on Tuesdays, he added.
